ai_summary: Scotland continues to demonstrate deep decarbonisation, recording an ultra-low carbon intensity of 6 gCO2/kWh compared to 186 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Scottish wind output currently stands at an estimated 2.2 GW, representing 21.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity, contributing significantly to the overall GB wind output of 3.8 GW. Despite this clean generation, cross-border transmission bottlenecks continue to limit power transfer to southern demand centres. System operators have curtailed 9,958 MWh of Scottish generation so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £379,714. Consequently, to balance demand, thermal generation was dispatched south of the constraint boundary, resulting in an estimated 1,892,077 m3 of gas burned elsewhere to replace it and adding 3,485 tonnes of CO2 emissions. Extrapolating these balancing actions gives an estimated total yearly cost of £139 million for curtailment. Recovered across Great Britain's annual electricity demand, this adds an estimated £0.5/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the direct financial and environmental cost of existing transmission boundary limitations.
